================================================

Implementation recap
--------------------
  def sort_list(items):
      result = list(items)                    # O1 concerns this copy
      for i in range(1, len(result)):         # outer loop over i
          key = result[i]
          j = i - 1
          while j >= 0 and result[j] > key:   # inner shift loop
              result[j + 1] = result[j]
              j -= 1
          result[j + 1] = key
      return result

Goal (from formal_spec.txt):
  forall L. Sorted(sort_list(L)) and Perm(L, sort_list(L))

We prove the stronger inductive statement by proving the obligations
below; the final theorem follows by taking the state at loop exit.


Obligation 1 -- Copy yields a permutation (base permutation fact)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
  O1: forall L. Perm(L, copy(L))
      where copy(L) is the list produced by `result = list(items)`.

  Proof idea: copy is an elementwise copy; occ(x, copy(L)) = occ(x, L)
  for every x, by induction on the length of L (appending preserves
  occurrence counts).


Obligation 2 -- Outer loop preserves permutation (permutation preservation)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  O2: If Perm(L, result) holds before one outer-loop iteration (state
      for index i), and the iteration transforms result into result'
      (inner shift loop plus key placement), then Perm(L, result')
      holds after the iteration.

  Sub-obligation 2a -- inner shift preserves permutation:
    O2a: If Perm(L, M) and M' is obtained from M by setting
         M'[j+1] = M[j] (right shift) for a fixed j, then Perm(L, M').
    Proof idea: the multiset of M' equals the multiset of M because
    the shifted element is duplicated then overwritten; more precisely
    occ(x, M') = occ(x, M) for all x, by case analysis on the positions
    j, j+1 and all other positions (which are unchanged).

  Sub-obligation 2b -- key placement preserves permutation:
    O2b: If Perm(L, M) holds for the state after the inner loop, and
         result' is obtained by result'[j+1] = key where key was the
         value removed from position i at the start of the iteration
         (result[i] = key, and positions i+1.. are untouched, position
         i is overwritten by the shift), then Perm(L, result').
    Proof idea: over the whole iteration, the multiset of the segment
    [0..i] is unchanged: the key is taken out of the multiset and put
    back exactly once; all other writes are the shifts of O2a.

  Together O1 + O2 (iterated over all outer iterations) give:
    Perm(L, sort_list(L)).

  outer iteration i had:

    P2: key = the original result[i] (value saved before shifting)
    P3: result[i] currently holds the value of result[i-1] (already

  the list still satisfies Perm (by O2a) and:
    INV1: result[0..j] is sorted and all elements of result[0..j]
          are <= key  (so the loop guard result[j] > key is exactly
          the condition to keep shifting)
    INV2: result[j+2..i] are all equal to key (they are copies of the
          shifted values), so the multiset is preserved.

  iteration and is bounded below by -1, so the inner loop terminates.
    O3-term: j is a termination measure for the inner loop.

---------------------------------------------------------

    INV3: result[0..i-1] is sorted (non-decreasing)
    INV4: Perm(L, result)  (carried from O1/O2)

  Base case: i = 1; result[0..0] is a single element, trivially sorted
  (base case of the induction).

  Inductive step: assuming INV3 and INV4 for i, after the iteration
  (inner shift loop + key placement) the list satisfies INV3 for i+1:
  result[0..i] is sorted.
    Proof idea: by the inner-loop invariant, the shift loop stops at
    the first position j with result[j] <= key (or at j = -1); the key
    is placed at j+1; elements left of j+1 are <= key (INV1), elements
    right of j+1 up to i are >= key (they are >= key by the guard
    condition), and result[i+1..] were already >= all of result[0..i]
    by the previous invariant; hence result[0..i] is sorted.

  This is the inductive step of the main induction on i.

----------------------------------------------
  O5: At loop exit (i = |result| = |L|), INV3 gives
        result[0..|L|-1] is sorted,
      which is exactly Sorted(sort_list(L)) (adjacent-pair form).
  Combined with INV4 (Perm(L, result)) we obtain the goal:
        Sorted(sort_list(L)) and Perm(L, sort_list(L)).


Obligation 6 -- Termination of the outer loop
---------------------------------------------
  O6: i ranges over 1..|result|, increasing by 1 each iteration, and
  |result| is fixed by the copy step, so the outer loop terminates.
  (Needed so that sort_list actually returns a value and O5 applies
  to the returned list.)


Summary of the proof structure
------------------------------
  O1 (copy permutes)                 -> Perm base
  O2a, O2b (iteration preserves Perm) -> Perm induction
  O3   (inner invariant + variant)    -> inner loop soundness & termination
  O4   (outer invariant)              -> sortedness induction
                                          (base: single element; step: O4)
  O5   (exit condition)               -> final theorem
  O6   (outer variant)                -> overall termination

{"content":"Proof Obligations for sort_list (insertion sort)
================================================

Implementation recap
--------------------
  def sort_list(items):
      result = list(items)                    # copy; OB1 concerns this
      for i in range(1, len(result)):         # outer loop, i = 1..n-1
          key = result[i]                     # key held OUT of the array
          j = i - 1
          while j >= 0 and result[j] > key:   # inner shift loop
              result[j + 1] = result[j]
              j -= 1
          result[j + 1] = key                 # key written back: Perm restored
      return result

Goal (from formal_spec.txt):
  forall L. Sorted(sort_list(L)) and Perm(L, sort_list(L))

Notation: a_0..a_{n-1} denote the elements of the input L; |L| = n.
"sorted(s, e)" means result[s..e] is non-decreasing.


Loop invariants
---------------
INV-OUT(i)  (before outer iteration i, 1 <= i <= n):
  (A) Perm(L, result)               -- multiset equality with the input
  (B) sorted(0, i-1)                -- prefix of length i is sorted
  (C) result[p] = a_p for all p >= i -- suffix untouched so far

INV-IN(j)  (at the inner-loop guard, during outer iteration i,
            with key = a_i saved before any shift):
  (1) multiset(result) = multiset(L) - {key} + {result[j+1]}
        -- "hole accounting": key is held out; position j+1 is the
           hole, currently holding a duplicate of the shifted values
           (or key itself, if no shift has happened yet, j+1 = i)
  (2) result[0..j] = a_0..a_j  and  sorted(0, j)
  (3) result[j+2..i] = a_{j+1}..a_{i-1}  (the displaced prefix elements,
        still in their original sorted order), hence sorted(j+2, i)
        and every one of them > key
  (4) result[p] = a_p for all p >= i+1


Obligations
-----------

OB1  (Copy yields a permutation -- base permutation fact)
  After `result = list(items)`:
    Perm(L, result)  and  result[p] = a_p for all 0 <= p < n.
  Proof: elementwise copy; occ(x, copy(L)) = occ(x, L) for all x.

OB2  (Inner invariant establishment)
  At the start of outer iteration i (1 <= i < n), from INV-OUT(i)
  and key = result[i] = a_i, j = i-1: INV-IN(i-1) holds.
  Checks: (1) hole is position i, holding key itself, so
  multiset(result) = multiset(L) - {key} + {key} = multiset(L);
  (2) prefix a_0..a_{i-1} sorted by INV-OUT(i).B; (3) range j+2..i
  is empty; (4) suffix by INV-OUT(i).C.

OB3  (Inner invariant preservation -- shift step)
  If INV-IN(j) and the guard holds (j >= 0 and result[j] > key),
  then after `result[j+1] = result[j]; j -= 1`, INV-IN(j-1) holds.
  Proof sketch:
    - (1): the write replaces the hole content a_{j+1} (duplicated
      one slot up) by a_j; the new hole is at (j-1)+1 = j. Multiset
      changes by -{a_{j+1}} + {a_j} on both sides.
    - (2): positions 0..j-1 untouched, still a_0..a_{j-1}, sorted.
    - (3): new displaced region j+1..i = a_j followed by the old
      a_{j+1}..a_{i-1}; sorted since a_j <= a_{j+1} (original prefix
      sorted), and a_j > key by the guard.
    - (4): untouched.
  Termination (variant): j strictly decreases and is bounded below
  by -1 (guard requires j >= 0), so the inner loop terminates.

OB4  (Inner exit -- key placement restores Perm and extends sortedness)
  If INV-IN(j) and the guard fails (j < 0 or result[j] <= key), then
  after `result[j+1] = key`, INV-OUT(i+1) holds:
    - (A) Perm: by (1), the multiset is multiset(L) - {key} +
      {result[j+1]}; the write replaces that hole value by key,
      restoring exactly multiset(L).
    - (B) sorted(0, i): head result[0..j] is sorted with all elements
      <= key (at exit result[j] <= key and the head is sorted; empty
      when j < 0); key sits at j+1; tail result[j+2..i] is sorted with
      all elements > key by (3). Edge case j+1 = i (no shift): the
      write is a no-op and sortedness of 0..i follows from the guard
      failure result[i-1] <= key alone.
    - (C) suffix: shifts and the write only touch positions <= i.
  This obligation discharges permutation preservation (with OB1, OB3)
  and the inductive step for sortedness.

OB5  (Outer base case)
  INV-OUT(1) holds on loop entry: (A) by OB1; (B) sorted(0, 0) is
  trivial (single element); (C) by OB1. Degenerate inputs n <= 1
  never enter the loop, and OB1 + trivial sortedness give the
  postcondition directly.

OB6  (Outer inductive step)
  For 1 <= i < n: INV-OUT(i) implies INV-OUT(i+1).
  Proof: OB2 establishes INV-IN, OB3 preserves it around the inner
  loop, OB4 closes the iteration. This is the main induction on i.

OB7  (Postcondition at outer exit)
  At loop exit i = n: INV-OUT(n) gives sorted(0, n-1), i.e.
  Sorted(sort_list(L)), and Perm(L, result), i.e.
  Perm(L, sort_list(L)). Together with OB5 this proves the goal.

OB8  (Termination)
  Outer variant: n - i strictly decreases each iteration and is
  bounded below by 0, so the outer loop terminates and sort_list
  returns (needed for OB7 to apply to the returned list).


Summary of the proof structure
------------------------------
  OB1  copy permutes                  -> Perm base
  OB2  inner invariants established   -> links outer/inner loops
  OB3  shift preserves invariants     -> inner inductive step (+ inner
                                          termination variant)
  OB4  exit restores Perm, extends sorted prefix
                                      -> permutation preservation and
                                         sortedness inductive step
  OB5  base case i = 1                -> sortedness base case
  OB6  outer inductive step           -> INV-OUT(i) for all i
  OB7  postcondition                  -> final theorem
  OB8  outer termination              -> totality of sort_list
","path":"sorting_verification/obligations.txt"}
